summary.text: A 42-year-old man with bipolar affective disorder and hypertension presented to the emergency department 90 minutes after an intentional overdose of 60 g of extended-release valproic acid with co-ingested zolpidem 110 mg and paracetamol 2 g. He was drowsy and hypotensive with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 10, and was intubated and mechanically ventilated for depressed consciousness and persistent hypoxia.

Valproic acid exceeded 450 µg/mL and ammonia was 76 µmol/L. Chest radiograph showed bilateral basal pneumonitis and pleural effusions, brain CT was unremarkable, and abdominal radiograph showed no radio-opaque foreign bodies, but abdominal CT showed radiolucent foreign bodies and upper endoscopy confirmed a 30-cm clumped pharmacobezoar of VPA tablets in the stomach.

Management included activated charcoal followed by multiple-dose activated charcoal, naloxone, L-carnitine, toxicology and gastroenterology consultation, and continuous renal replacement therapy in the intensive care unit after he met EXTRIP criteria with serial monitoring. VPA fell below 2.8 µg/mL and ammonia normalized; he was extubated on day 5 and transferred to the ward on day 11 in stable condition.

During admission he developed bilateral limb weakness, rigidity, tremor, rotatory nystagmus and clonus. EEG and brain MRI were normal, initial nerve conduction was unremarkable, repeat testing showed ulnar sensory neuropathy and EMG showed myopathic features with active denervation. Toxic myopathy with EPS was diagnosed and procyclidine started; he was transferred to inpatient rehabilitation and discharged ambulatory after 54 days.

article_limitations: Table 2 (segments b00051-b00120) and the discussion of published reports describe other patients in the literature; none are roster patients or index-patient facts.

Figure 3 printed data labels are transcribed only in the visual review; they are not source-text evidence and are not recorded as facts. Their timing differs from the text's VPA fall below 2.8 µg/mL over 72 hours and their first point lacks Table 1's > comparator; both are recorded as ambiguities.
Table 1 day labels: the lab rows are governed by the caption day 1 of admission, while Figure 3 labels the first reading Day 0; day numbering is not reconciled.
The discharge after 54 days has no stated start point; no rehabilitation facility details are given.
The initial history was incomplete and relied on collateral family information; no further detail is stated.
Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; actual JPEGs are inspected in the separate visual target.
No supplementary files are listed for this article.
